items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: We had a guy in the band named Brent Sparks who contacted a fella who owned a filling station and this man was I believe a Mason.

ctx.x: And the best we could do was just make enough to buy cigarettes and eat and buy gasoline. And so we scuffled and got ourselves together and we moved back east. Went through Little Rock, Arkansas, that's my home, I had a chance to see my people. Jeter had a chance to see his people. We hung around Little Rock several days, we played a little dance there, made a little money, and we moved on up -- we made it as far as Delaware, Ohio.

We couldn't go any farther. We had a guy in the band named Brent Sparks who contacted a fella who owned a filling station and this man was I believe a Mason. And this man came to the rescue of Brent Sparks and us, we got enough money to get into Cleveland, Ohio. We got back into Cleveland, Ohio and was able to borrow enough money to get us to Syracuse, New York. Jeter was driving a Model A Ford, three of us were riding with him. We had our instruments packed in the back in the rumble seat. The rumble seat could…

So we had been booked into a pocket. And there we were in Syracuse, New York, where no work, and that's when Stuff Smith left the band and went back to Buffalo, where his wife was. A. G. Godley Bartley left the band and went back to Cleveland, where his wife was. So the band almost broke up there in Syracuse, Peanuts Peter Holland stuck with the band, we had the reed section stuck with the band, Snub Mosley that Bosely stuck with the band, Crook, the banjo player, stuck with the band.
